scenarios.name: single, lower income, no age threshold or phase-out exists so cases vary income instead of age
scenarios.source: Alaska has no individual income tax and therefore no form to derive a figure from. Primary source: Alaska Department of Revenue, Tax Division, Personal Income Tax program page. The page asks and answers its own question: 'Does Alaska have a personal income tax? The State of Alaska currently does not have an individual income tax, therefore no employee withholding for state income tax is required.' expectedStateTax = $0 follows directly from that sentence, for any income composition. This case is a single filer with pension income only. Alaska's retirementExemptions config (pensionExemption/iraWithdrawalExemption both 'full', socialSecurityExempt true) is inert here because taxSystem.noIncomeTax already zeroes the result before any exemption is applied (TaxCalculationEngine.swift:396). No age threshold or AGI phase-out exists in Alaska law, so per the batch matrix rule this case and the next vary income rather than age.

scenarios.name: single, higher income including a Roth conversion, no age threshold or phase-out exists so cases vary income instead of age
scenarios.source: Same primary source as the prior case: Alaska DOR Personal Income Tax program page, 'The State of Alaska currently does not have an individual income tax.' This case raises income well above the prior one and adds an IRA withdrawal and a Roth conversion, exactly the kind of income a multi-year conversion plan produces, to confirm the $0 result holds regardless of composition, not just for plain pension income.

scenarios.name: MFJ, both spouses present, moderate combined income including Social Security
scenarios.source: Same primary source: Alaska DOR Personal Income Tax program page confirms no individual income tax exists, for any filing status. This is the MFJ 'both spouses qualifying' case in the batch matrix; because Alaska has no age-gated exemption there is nothing to qualify for, so both spouses are simply present with retirement ages. Income mix adds taxable Social Security to the pension/IRA combination exercised in the single cases.

scenarios.name: MFJ, only one spouse retirement-aged, highest combined income in the batch
scenarios.source: Same primary source: Alaska DOR Personal Income Tax program page. This is the batch's 'MFJ, only one spouse qualifying' case; Alaska has no per-spouse age gate for its (nonexistent) income tax, so there is no attribution rule to trip, but the case is included anyway per the matrix so a later phase adding an age gate has a case waiting. Highest income in the batch (pension + IRA withdrawal + Roth conversion) to stress the largest plausible single-year total against the $0 expectation.
